title: A deactivation refused after the save keeps the confirmation open
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create an active part, part A, for this test with a Sell Price of $20.00.
  • Use a desktop browser that can open a second tab on the same ShopView address, signed in as the same user.
  • Start in browser tab 1 on the Inventory page, on the Active tab, with part A's part number typed in the Search box.
custom_steps:
1. In tab 1, click the part A row.
  2. In tab 1, replace the Sell Price with 25.00.
  3. In tab 1, click Inactive under Part Status.
  4. Open a second browser tab on the same ShopView address.
  5. In tab 2, click Parts in the top bar.
  6. In tab 2, click Inventory in the left menu.
  7. In tab 2, type part A's part number in the Search box.
  8. In tab 2, click the part A row.
  9. In tab 2, click Inactive under Part Status.
  10. In tab 2, click Save.
  11. In tab 2, click Deactivate in the confirmation.
  12. Switch back to tab 1 without reloading it.
  13. In tab 1, click Save.
  14. In tab 1, click Deactivate in the confirmation.
  15. Wait 10 seconds.
  16. Click Close on the red message.
  17. In tab 1, click Cancel in the confirmation.
  18. In tab 1, click Cancel in Edit Inventory Part.
  19. In tab 1, click the Inactive tab.
  20. In tab 1, click the part A row.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A in tab 1.

Step 2:

  • Sell Price shows 25.00.

Step 3:

  • Inactive is selected.

Step 4:

  • A second tab opens.

Step 5:

  • Tab 2 shows the Parts left menu.

Step 6:

  • Tab 2 shows the Inventory page.

Step 7:

  • Part A is listed in tab 2.

Step 8:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens in tab 2.

Step 9:

  • Inactive is selected in tab 2.

Step 10:

  • The "Deactivate part?" confirmation opens in tab 2.

Step 11:

  • Tab 2 shows "Part deactivated.": part A is now inactive.

Step 12:

  • Tab 1 still shows the part window with Inactive picked.

Step 13:

  • The "Deactivate part?" confirmation opens in tab 1.

Step 14:

  • The confirmation stays open, and a red message reads "This part could not be deactivated" with the reason "Part is already in that state."

Step 15:

  • The red message is still showing after 10 seconds: it stays until it is closed.

Step 16:

  • The red message closes.

Step 17:

  • The confirmation closes.

Step 18:

  • The part window closes.

Step 19:

  • The Inactive tab lists part A.

Step 20:

  • The title row pill reads "Inactive" and Sell Price reads 25.00: the form was saved before the status change was refused.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog), story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change)

  • S13-N4: “If the status change is refused after the save, the confirmation stays open and the system shows "This part could not be deactivated" or "This part could not be activated", with the reason.”
  • S13-R22: “Confirming saves every change in the dialog, then applies the status, and closes the dialog with "Part deactivated." or "Part activated.".”
  • S10-R13a: “The reasons are "A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead.", "Part not found." and "Part is already in that state."”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Status change from the part dialog refused | "This part could not be deactivated" / "This part could not be activated", with the reason | Error toast, stays until closed”
